A velocity field assigns a velocity vector to every position and time in a moving continuum. Its spatial derivatives describe local deformation, rotation, and volume change.

which interpolates among objective convected derivatives as the dimensionless slip parameter a changes.
Retardation time of an Oldroyd fluid (λ2​)
Words: 26
Johnson--Segalman--Oldroyd model OurBigBook.com
The retardation time controls the delayed strain-rate term in an Oldroyd constitutive equation. Together with the relaxation time it determines the solvent-like high-frequency or high-rate response.
Linear oscillatory response of a Johnson--Segalman--Oldroyd fluid
Words: 7
Johnson--Segalman--Oldroyd model OurBigBook.com
In small-amplitude oscillatory shear,
G′=1+ω2λ12​ηω2(λ1​−λ2​)​,G′′=1+ω2λ12​ηω(1+ω2λ1​λ2​)​.
(173)
Steady shear viscosity of a Johnson--Segalman--Oldroyd fluid (ηsh​)
Words: 21
Johnson--Segalman--Oldroyd model OurBigBook.com
For Gordon--Schowalter parameter 0<a<2, the steady shear viscosity is
ηsh​=η1+a(2−a)λ12​γ˙​21+a(2−a)λ1​λ2​γ˙​2​.
(174)
It is shear thinning when λ1​>λ2​.
Normal-stress difference
Words: 14
Viscoelasticity OurBigBook.com
In simple shear, the first and second normal-stress differences are N1​=τxx​−τyy​ and N2​=τyy​−τzz​.
Extensional viscosity (ηext​)
Words: 53 Articles: 2
Viscoelasticity OurBigBook.com
The uniaxial extensional viscosity is the tensile normal-stress difference divided by the imposed extension rate.
Uniaxial extensional flow
Words: 17
Extensional viscosity OurBigBook.com
An incompressible uniaxial extensional flow has velocity u=ϵ˙(−x/2,−y/2,z). Its principal deformation rates are −ϵ˙/2,−ϵ˙/2,ϵ˙.
Trouton ratio
Words: 21
Extensional viscosity OurBigBook.com
The Trouton ratio is extensional viscosity divided by shear viscosity. It approaches three for an incompressible Newtonian fluid in uniaxial extension.

Suspension rheology

Words: 94 Articles: 3
Non-Newtonian fluid OurBigBook.com
Suspension rheology relates particle concentration, particle pressure, shear stress, deformation rate, and fluid migration in a mixture of particles and a liquid.
Jamming
Words: 25
Suspension rheology OurBigBook.com
Jamming is the loss of the ability of a dense disordered material to flow as its particle fraction or applied confinement reaches a critical state.
Viscous number (Iv​)
Words: 15
Suspension rheology OurBigBook.com
The viscous number Iv​=η∣γ˙​∣/ps​ compares viscous shear stress with particle pressure in a dense suspension.
Shear-induced dilation
Words: 32
Suspension rheology OurBigBook.com
Shear-induced dilation is the tendency of a dense granular or suspended-particle packing to increase its volume under shear. In a saturated confined system it requires pore-fluid migration and can delay stress adjustment.

Porous-media flow

Words: 385 Articles: 11
Fluid mechanics OurBigBook.com
Porous-media flow is fluid motion through an interconnected pore space. At small pore-scale Reynolds number, its volume-averaged velocity is commonly governed by Darcy's law.

Unconfined aquifer

Words: 178 Articles: 4
Porous-media flow OurBigBook.com
An unconfined aquifer has a free groundwater table. In a shallow aquifer of thickness h(x,t), hydrostatic pressure and Darcy's law give horizontal flux proportional to −hhx​.

Boussinesq equation for an unconfined aquifer

Words: 78 Articles: 1
Unconfined aquifer OurBigBook.com
For pore fraction n, permeability k, liquid density ρ, viscosity μ, rainfall recharge R, and a shallow groundwater thickness h,
nht​=μkρg​(hhx​)x​+R.
(175)
This is a nonlinear diffusion equation with diffusivity proportional to the local thickness.
Separable aquifer drawdown
Words: 36
Boussinesq equation for an unconfined aquifer OurBigBook.com
After recharge stops on a finite aquifer connected to a river, the late solution of the Boussinesq equation for an unconfined aquifer has the form h∼t−1F(x/L). The profile solves a nonlinear eigenvalue problem, and river discharge decays as t−2.

Poroelastic aquifer

Words: 74 Articles: 1
Unconfined aquifer OurBigBook.com
A poroelastic aquifer couples pore-fluid storage and flow to elastic compaction of its solid skeleton. Changes in gravity, surface loading, or pore pressure can therefore change groundwater discharge even without changing rainfall.
Poroelastic compaction length (ℓc​)
Words: 42
Poroelastic aquifer OurBigBook.com
For a skeleton with Young modulus E, undeformed solid fraction ϕ0​, grain-fluid density difference ρs​−ρ, and reference gravity g0​, the hydrostatic poroelastic compaction length is
ℓc​=ϕ0​(ρs​−ρ)g0​E​.
(176)
It is the depth over which self-weight changes the solid fraction appreciably.

Darcy law

Words: 112 Articles: 3
Porous-media flow OurBigBook.com
Darcy's law gives the relative seepage velocity through a porous packing as uf​−us​=−(k/η)∇p, where k is permeability.

Saffman–Taylor instability

Words: 31
Darcy law OurBigBook.com
The Saffman–Taylor instability occurs when a more mobile fluid displaces a less mobile fluid in a porous medium or Hele–Shaw cell. Viscosity contrast amplifies interface corrugations, while surface tension suppresses sufficiently short wavelengths.

Permeability of a porous medium (k)

Words: 30
Darcy law OurBigBook.com
The permeability of a porous medium measures its ability to transmit fluid. In Darcy's law, k has dimensions of area and depends on the geometry and connectivity of the pore space.

Pressure-dependent Darcy drainage

Words: 30
Darcy law OurBigBook.com
Suppose a porous layer has thickness h(p) and permeability of a porous medium k(p), and the pressure drop p acts across its thickness. Darcy's law gives the drainage volume flux
w=μh(p)k(p)​p.
(177)
If k/h=Kp−β, then w=(K/μ)p1−β.

Porous gravity current

Words: 71 Articles: 1
Porous-media flow OurBigBook.com
A porous gravity current spreads because a density difference creates a lateral hydrostatic-pressure gradient. For a two-dimensional current of thickness h, density deficit Δρ, permeability k, viscosity μ, and porosity ϕ,
ϕht​=μkΔρg​(hhx​)x​.
(178)

Leaky porous gravity current

Words: 31
Porous gravity current OurBigBook.com
A leaky porous gravity current loses flux through a localized fracture or a distributed permeable boundary. At a point fracture, mass conservation makes the horizontal Darcy flux discontinuous by exactly the leakage rate.

Reduced gravity (g′)

Words: 354 Articles: 11
Fluid mechanics OurBigBook.com
For two Boussinesq fluids with density difference Δρ and reference density ρ0​, reduced gravity is g′=gΔρ/ρ0​.

Entraining shallow-water layer

Words: 36
Reduced gravity OurBigBook.com
An entraining shallow-water layer changes depth, density, and momentum as ambient fluid crosses its interface. Entrainment dilutes its reduced gravity and accelerates or decelerates it through the momentum needed to bring new fluid into the layer.

Gravity current

Words: 300 Articles: 9
Reduced gravity OurBigBook.com
A gravity current is a predominantly horizontal flow driven by a density difference. Its front speed scales as the square root of reduced gravity times current depth.

Froude number (Fr)

Words: 46 Articles: 1
Gravity current OurBigBook.com
The Froude number compares inertial speed with a gravity-wave speed. For a shallow gravity current of depth h and reduced gravity g′, Fr=U/g′h​.
Gravity-current front condition
Words: 25
Froude number OurBigBook.com
A common high-Reynolds number closure for a deep-ambient gravity current is L˙=Frg′h​, where L is front position and the order-one Froude number depends on the chosen front model.

Gravity-current box model

Words: 125 Articles: 3
Gravity current OurBigBook.com
A gravity-current box model replaces the current by a well-mixed region with uniform depth and density. Integral volume, scalar, and front-speed balances then reduce the spreading problem to ordinary differential equations.
Detrainment-limited gravity-current runout
Words: 45
Gravity-current box model OurBigBook.com
If a finite-volume gravity current loses or dilutes the scalar that supplies its reduced gravity, its front can approach a finite runout length of a gravity current. A box model couples the scalar balance to a gravity-current front condition; eliminating time then gives the front position directly as a function of the remaining scalar concentration.
Particle-laden gravity current
Words: 51 Articles: 1
Gravity-current box model OurBigBook.com
A particle-laden gravity current is driven by the excess density of suspended particles. Deposition decreases its reduced gravity, so a finite-volume current can approach a finite runout length.
Runout length of a gravity current (L∞​)
Words: 24
Particle-laden gravity current OurBigBook.com
The runout length is the limiting horizontal distance reached by a gravity current after its driving buoyancy has been exhausted or balanced by resistance.

Draining gravity current

Words: 74 Articles: 1
Gravity current OurBigBook.com
A draining gravity current loses fluid through its substrate while spreading horizontally. For a two-dimensional viscous current of thickness H(x,t) that loses fluid according to pressure-dependent Darcy drainage,
Ht​=A(H3Hx​)x​−DH1−β,A=3μρg​,
(179)
when the hydrostatic pressure is p=ρgH and k/h∝p−β.
Similarity exponents of a draining gravity current
Words: 35
Draining gravity current OurBigBook.com
If a draining gravity current is supplied with volume flux proportional to tα, a first-kind similarity solution has
H=taF(x/tb),a=52α+1​,b=53α+4​,
(180)
provided
β=a1​=2α+15​.
(181)
These relations follow by balancing the time derivative, horizontal lubrication theory flux, vertical drainage, and imposed inlet flux.

Lock-exchange flow

Words: 28
Gravity current OurBigBook.com
Removing a barrier between fluids of different densities creates oppositely directed gravity currents. In an energy-conserving Boussinesq exchange through a full-depth opening, each layer occupies half the depth.

Laminar round jet

Words: 94 Articles: 2
Fluid mechanics OurBigBook.com
A laminar round jet is an axisymmetric momentum-driven flow issuing into otherwise still fluid. Viscous diffusion broadens the jet while its axial momentum flux remains constant.

Conserved momentum flux of a laminar round jet

Words: 44
Laminar round jet OurBigBook.com
For axial velocity w(r,z) in the boundary-layer approximation,
M=∫0∞​rw2dr
(182)
is independent of z. If W and δ are characteristic centre-line speed and width, then Wδ∼M1/2, while the momentum balance gives Wδ2∼νz. Thus
δ∼M1/2νz​,W∼νzM​.
(183)

Similarity solution for a laminar round jet

Words: 24
Laminar round jet OurBigBook.com
With axisymmetric streamfunction ψ=νzg(r/z), the regular normalized similarity profile is
g(η)=32ν2+3Mη212Mη2​.
(184)
Its volume flux grows linearly with z, expressing fluid entrainment.

Fluid entrainment

Words: 26
Fluid mechanics OurBigBook.com
Fluid entrainment is the incorporation of surrounding fluid into a moving current, jet, or plume. It increases volume flux while diluting transported momentum, buoyancy, or concentration.

Turbulent plume

Words: 435 Articles: 13
Fluid mechanics OurBigBook.com
A turbulent plume is a buoyancy-driven shear flow that grows by entraining ambient fluid.

Buoyancy flux (B)

Words: 26
Turbulent plume OurBigBook.com
The buoyancy flux through a section is the integral of velocity times reduced gravity. In a Boussinesq pure plume in a uniform ambient it is conserved.

Batchelor entrainment hypothesis

Words: 54 Articles: 1
Turbulent plume OurBigBook.com
Batchelor's entrainment hypothesis takes the mean normal entrainment velocity at a turbulent plume edge to be a constant fraction of a characteristic axial velocity.

Entrainment coefficient (α)

Words: 30
Batchelor entrainment hypothesis OurBigBook.com
The entrainment coefficient is the dimensionless constant in the Batchelor entrainment hypothesis, so the mean speed at which ambient fluid crosses a plume edge is α times the plume's characteristic axial speed.

Top-hat plume model

Words: 279 Articles: 7
Turbulent plume OurBigBook.com
A top-hat plume model takes velocity and reduced gravity to be uniform across the plume and zero outside it. Integral volume, momentum, and buoyancy fluxes then depend only on plume width and these uniform values.

Pure plume

Words: 246 Articles: 6
Top-hat plume model OurBigBook.com
A pure plume is a similarity regime in which the source supplies buoyancy flux but no dynamically persistent source volume or momentum flux. Its finite source region is represented by a plume virtual origin.
Axisymmetric pure plume
Words: 37
Pure plume OurBigBook.com
For a top-hat axisymmetric pure plume of radius r, speed U, and reduced gravity g′, the conserved fluxes are Q=πr2U, M=πr2U2, and B=πr2Ug′. The Batchelor entrainment hypothesis gives Q∝B1/3z5/3.
Line plume
Words: 149 Articles: 3
Pure plume OurBigBook.com
A line plume is invariant along one horizontal direction, so its integral fluxes are measured per unit span. A wall line plume entrains through one exposed edge and has width proportional to distance from its plume virtual origin.
Wall line plume
Words: 70 Articles: 1
Line plume OurBigBook.com
A wall line plume is a one-sided line plume adjoining a solid wall. Under a top-hat pure-plume model, d(bW)/ds=αW because only its outer edge entrains ambient fluid.
Triangular-profile wall line plume
Words: 44
Wall line plume OurBigBook.com
In a triangular-profile wall line plume, axial velocity and reduced gravity decrease linearly from their wall values to zero across the plume width b. If the wall speed is W, its volume and kinematic momentum fluxes per unit span are V=bW/2 and J=bW2/3.
Stratified line-plume height scale (zs​)
Words: 43
Line plume OurBigBook.com
A line plume of kinematic buoyancy flux B0​ rising through uniform buoyancy frequency N has the dimensional height scale
zs​=NB01/3​​.
(185)
It measures the height over which ambient stratification removes an order-one fraction of the plume buoyancy before the plume reaches neutral buoyancy and spreads as a buoyant intrusion.
Plume virtual origin
Words: 30
Pure plume OurBigBook.com
A plume virtual origin is the extrapolated point at which a similarity plume's width and volume flux vanish. It absorbs finite source geometry into a shift of the axial coordinate.

Heated wall plume

Words: 25
Turbulent plume OurBigBook.com
A heated wall plume is a one-sided plume adjacent to a wall. A uniform wall heat flux makes its buoyancy flux grow linearly with height.

Buoyant intrusion

Words: 37
Turbulent plume OurBigBook.com
A buoyant intrusion is a predominantly horizontal current formed when a rising or sinking plume reaches nearly neutral buoyancy in a stratified ambient fluid. The plume's momentum generally carries it beyond its neutral-buoyancy level before it spreads.

Natural ventilation

Words: 193 Articles: 5
Fluid mechanics OurBigBook.com
Natural ventilation exchanges indoor and outdoor fluid through openings using pressure differences created by buoyancy or wind.

Displacement ventilation

Words: 75 Articles: 1
Natural ventilation OurBigBook.com
Displacement ventilation supplies relatively cool air at low level and removes warmer air at high level. In the ideal two-layer model, buoyant plumes feed a warm upper layer above a sharp density interface while the supply occupies the lower layer.

Displacement-ventilation interface height (h)

Words: 35
Displacement ventilation OurBigBook.com
At steady state, the displacement-ventilation interface lies where the total plume volume flux equals the imposed ventilation flux. For one triangular-profile wall line plume with kinematic buoyancy flux B0​, entrainment coefficient α, and ventilation flux A per unit span,
h=(3α2​)2/3B01/3​A​.
(186)

Single-opening exchange flow

Words: 65 Articles: 1
Natural ventilation OurBigBook.com
A tall opening between fluids of different densities can support simultaneous inflow below a neutral pressure level and outflow above it. For a symmetric opening with a Boussinesq hydrostatic pressure difference and equal discharge coefficients, the neutral level lies at mid-height.

Neutral pressure level

Words: 24
Single-opening exchange flow OurBigBook.com
The neutral pressure level is the height at which indoor and outdoor hydrostatic pressures agree. Flow through an opening reverses direction across this level.

Stratified-room plume-exchange model

Words: 36
Natural ventilation OurBigBook.com
A stratified-room plume-exchange model balances the upward volume transported by a warm plume against downward transport by cold wall plumes. A global buoyancy balance relates the source flux to the buoyancy carried out through the vents.

Homologous spherical flow (u=q(t)r)

Words: 44 Articles: 1
Fluid mechanics OurBigBook.com
A homologous spherical flow has velocity proportional to radius. Its velocity gradient is q(t)I and its velocity divergence is 3q(t).

Self-similar ansatz

Words: 27
Homologous spherical flow OurBigBook.com
A self-similar ansatz expresses evolving fields through a dimensionless similarity coordinate such as x=r/R(t), reducing a partial differential equation to ordinary differential equations in x.
